reviewer: opus-5, review of folding ref_arch/new/ up and deriving the reference stack
numbering_note: tools/ceremony_next.py read 15 off disk. Paired with kb/ceremonies/ceremony-15-improve-89-reference-stack.json.
scope: ref_arch/ (the new/ fold), tools/extract_reference_stack.py, docs/reference/reference-stack.json, tools/phase.py, STATUS row 89.

findings.finding: The page could not render at all. Its component does `import('./cellplane-stack.js')` and that module was not in ref_arch/ -- it sat in an untracked ref_arch/new/ alongside fifteen other files, fourteen of which were byte-identical copies of what was already committed.
findings.evidence: sha256 comparison of ref_arch/new/ against ref_arch/: 14 identical, 1 differing (Reference Model.dc.html), 1 present only in new/ (cellplane-stack.js, 26420 bytes).
findings.found_by: owner pointed at the file; the missing import surfaced on reading it
findings.suggested_change: Move the two that differ up, delete the fourteen identical copies, remove new/.

findings.finding: The stack cites its own source -- "MVP-SCALE Open Standards & Open-Source Stack Alignment v3 (uploads/mvp-scale-open-stack-alignment-v3.md), 2026-09-11" -- and that file is not in the repository. So the artifact carries a dangling provenance claim, and under this repo's rule nothing may cite the stack as sourced evidence until it resolves.
findings.evidence: os.path.exists('ref_arch/uploads/mvp-scale-open-stack-alignment-v3.md') is False; ref_arch/uploads/ holds only the three glossary files.
findings.found_by: author, checking the cited source rather than believing it
findings.suggested_change: Either add the source document or mark every stack-derived claim proposed. This is the owner's to resolve; STATUS row 89 carries it.

findings.finding: The two owner artifacts disagree on one layer key. The model calls the ninth area `concerns`; the stack calls it `cross`. Eight of nine keys match exactly, the titles are identical and the positions are the same, so the join is unambiguous -- but an undeclared mapping is one nobody can dispute later.
findings.evidence: Side-by-side of the nine keys: entry, intake, agent, execute, assure, observe, improve, shared all match; cross vs concerns differ.
findings.found_by: the extractor's own join check, on first run
findings.suggested_change: Declare the alias in the extractor and echo it into the derived JSON, rather than normalising it away.

findings.finding: The existing helper closes a string on the first quote character it meets, so a single-quoted JS string containing an escaped apostrophe -- `the customer\'s OIDC provider`, which the stack data has -- would be cut in half. It has not bitten because the model source contains no escapes.
findings.evidence: split_args(): `if ch == quote: quote = None`, with no backslash handling.
findings.found_by: author, deciding whether to reuse it
findings.suggested_change: Do not reuse it here. A separate parser that handles escapes, with the reason recorded, rather than a silent second copy of a subtly wrong one.
